security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, vector load instructions (vle*.v, vlse*.v, vluxei*.v, vloxei*.v) are translated into host code that iterates over vector elements. When a guest page fault or access fault occurs at element index N during this iteration, QEMU's generated host code may have already written loaded data to destination vector register elements at indices > N before the exception is delivered. If QEMU does not precisely match the hardware's policy for VECTOR_LOAD_PAST_TRAP (whether elements past the trap index are clobbered or preserved), the guest exception handler will observe vector register state that differs from real silicon. Conversely, if QEMU preserves elements past the trap (the safe default for TCG) but the guest kernel was tested on hardware that clobbers them, guest software may incorrectly rely on QEMU's 'cleaner' state and leak sensitive kernel data across privilege boundaries after an mmap'd page fault on vector loads.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: TCG vector load helper that writes to vreg before or without checking for memory access faults per element; gen_helper_vle_v or similar helpers that batch-write destination vector registers independently of trap delivery order; missing post-trap vector register element restoration in HELPER(vle*_v) implementations in target/riscv/vector_helper.c
security_spec.summary: QEMU TCG vector load emulation may leak data through destination vector register elements written past the faulting index before a memory exception is delivered, violating guest kernel expectations about observable architectural state after page faults

findings.finding: Each vector element load writes immediately and directly to the destination vector register array via '*cur = cpu_##LDSUF##_data_ra(env, addr, retaddr)'. The RISC-V spec norm:vector_ls_overwrite_past_trap explicitly permits load instructions to overwrite active destination elements past the trap index. This is the correct implementation-defined behavior that matches real hardware implementations that pipeline or speculatively execute vector element loads.

spec_citations.excerpt: Load instructions may overwrite active destination vector register group elements past the element index at which the trap is reported.

findings.finding: Strided vector load writes each element to vd immediately and incrementally updates env->vstart (line 322: 'env->vstart = ++i'). On a page fault at element N, env->vstart is correctly positioned at N for restart. Per spec norm:vstart_op, re-execution begins from vstart, leaving earlier elements undisturbed and correctly overwriting any clobbered elements at or past vstart. The design satisfies the precise trap requirement: elements preceding vstart have committed results, and elements at or following vstart may have been updated but re-execution correctly overwrites them (norm:V_precise_traps relaxation at lines 4983-4986).

spec_citations.excerpt: All vector instructions are defined to begin execution with the element number given in the vstart CSR, leaving earlier elements in the destination vector undisturbed, and to reset the vstart CSR to zero at the end of execution.

We relax the last requirement to allow elements following vstart to have been updated at the time the trap is reported, provided that re-executing the instruction from the given vstart will correctly overwrite those elements.

findings.finding: Indexed vector load (used by both vluxei and vloxei) follows the same vstart tracking and immediate-write pattern as strided loads. Elements are written directly to vd one at a time (line 615). On fault, vstart captures the faulting element index, and restart re-executes from that point. Compliant with the spec's precise trap model.

spec_citations.excerpt: The V vector extension has precise traps.

findings.finding: Two distinct code paths with different overwrite-past-trap behaviors. The fast host path (flags==0) uses vext_continuous_ldst_host which, for esz==1, performs a single memcpy writing ALL elements atomically (lines 271-276). The slow TLB path writes elements sequentially with per-element fault detection (lines 411-424). On fast path, if a fault were to occur (TOCTOU race or cosmic ray), elements past the fault are already written to vreg. On slow path, elements past the fault are NOT written (the loop stops at the fault point). While both behaviors are spec-compliant (VECTOR_LS_OVERWRITE_PAST_TRAP permits overwriting), the inconsistency between paths could mask guest kernel bugs that depend on specific post-trap register state. In single-threaded TCG the race is not practically exploitable, but the divergence should be documented.

spec_citations.excerpt: Load instructions may overwrite active destination vector register group elements past the element index at which the trap is reported.

findings.finding: Fault-only-first vector load (vle8ff-vle64ff) correctly pre-probes all element addresses before loading any data (lines 709-747). On the first element (i==0), probe_pages is called with nonfault=false to allow synchronous exceptions. On subsequent elements, nonfault probes detect inaccessible pages and trim vl (lines 726-737). Only after vl is trimmed does the actual data loading begin (lines 754-801). This correctly implements norm:vector_ff_op — if element 0 faults, vl is unchanged and trap is taken; if element > 0 would fault, vl is reduced and no trap is taken. Elements past the new vl are set by vext_set_tail_elems_1s. No data is loaded past the trimmed vl.

spec_citations.excerpt: If element 0 raises an exception, vl is not modified, and the trap is taken. If an element > 0 raises an exception, the corresponding trap is not taken, and the vector length vl is reduced to the index of the element that would have raised an exception.

findings.finding: Ordered (vloxei*) and unordered (vluxei*) indexed loads are decoded identically to the same vlxei*_v helpers. The funct3 bit pattern '0-1' accepts both variants (line 399). The spec distinguishes these: unordered loads allow arbitrary element access order, while ordered loads must access elements in element order. QEMU translates both to the same vext_ldst_index() helper which accesses elements in sequential order. While this is functionally correct (sequential order satisfies both ordered and unordered semantics), it means QEMU does not model the relaxed memory ordering that real hardware may exploit for vluxei. This could mask guest software bugs that depend on specific memory ordering behavior of unordered indexed loads.

Vector register state is fully included in migration: VMSTATE_UINT64_ARRAY(env.vreg, ...) covers all 32 vector registers at RV_VLEN_MAX/64 = 1024/64 = 16 uint64_t per register, for 512 total uint64_t entries. All control state (vxrm, vxsat, vl, vstart, vtype, vill) is also migrated. The vector_needed() gate correctly checks for RVV extension (KVM) or ext_zve32x (TCG). No vector state is missing from migration.

VMSTATE_UINT64_ARRAY(env.vreg, RISCVCPU, 32 * RV_VLEN_MAX / 64),
VMSTATE_UINTTL(env.vxrm, RISCVCPU),

VMSTATE_UINTTL(env.vl, RISCVCPU),

findings.finding: The fault-only-first load translation correctly handles that vl may be modified by the helper. After the helper call, gen_update_pc advances the PC and lookup_and_goto_ptr exits the TB to re-translate with the updated vl value (lines 1141-1143). s->base.is_jmp is set to DISAS_NORETURN to prevent further translation in the current TB. This is the correct pattern for instructions that modify vl during execution.

The VSTART_CHECK_EARLY_EXIT macro correctly handles the case where vstart >= vl (all elements already processed on restart). It resets vstart to 0 and returns immediately. This implements the spec requirement that an instruction that has completed all elements (vstart == vl) does nothing and resets vstart to 0. No destination registers are modified in this case.

spec_citations.excerpt: All vector instructions are defined to begin execution with the element number given in the vstart CSR... and to reset the vstart CSR to zero at the end of execution.
